digest.component_or_area: LLM frontier fallback chain and failure classification
propositions: Under concurrent multi-session load the shared Bedrock account throttles (429 rate-limit), which is classified as retryable (WAIT_AND_RETRY), yet review-plan returns INDETERMINATE fleet-wide because the throttle triggers failover to a keyless anthropic:opus fallback.

The keyless fallback raises TypeError(Could not resolve authentication method), which has should_fall_back predicate=False, causing pydantic-ai 1.107.2 to bare-reraise the TypeError and discard the primary's retained retryable 429 instead of building a FallbackExceptionGroup.

classify_llm_failure(TypeError) maps to NEEDS_INVESTIGATION (non-retryable) instead of preserving the primary's WAIT_AND_RETRY, converting a benign retryable throttle into a hard non-retryable INDETERMINATE verdict.
Even if a FallbackExceptionGroup were produced, the blanket classification arm maps it to CHANGE_PROVIDER_OR_MODEL without inspecting individual leg dispositions, masking the retryable primary.

The fix marks non-primary fallback-leg exceptions with _FALLBACK_LEG_ATTR (stamped in _TracedCandidateModel.request when _candidate_order > 0) so should_fall_back always retains them into the group, and classify_llm_failure routes groups through _classify_fallback_group to return the most-recoverable (retryable) disposition.

Fleet-wide simultaneity arises from the shared account throttle; local host health and independent sessions are unrelated to the root cause, which is the disposition-masking in the fallback chain under a keyless configuration.
